schema_notes.logical_structure: ANY (single OR-group, any one option satisfies it) | ALL (every listed concept independently required -- N separate rows) | MIXED (an ALL-level combination of ANY-groups and/or single concepts, e.g. '(Python or Java) and SQL') | AMBIGUOUS (English genuinely supports more than one reading; no single structure is the one correct answer) | NONE (not a technology enumeration at all)
schema_notes.exhaustive_or_illustrative: exhaustive (the posting's own list IS the complete acceptable set) | illustrative (the list is introduced by an explicit example cue -- '(e.g., ...)' / 'such as' -- and a technology outside the list may also satisfy the real-world requirement, though this project's parser has no mechanism to award credit for an unlisted technology and is not expected to gain one here) | n/a (logical_structure is NONE)
schema_notes.conservative_fallback_expected: What a SAFE implementation must do when the full structure cannot be represented: 'any_of_group' (one JobRequirement, alternative_concept_ids populated) | 'independent_rows' (one JobRequirement per distinct concept -- correct for true ALL) | 'unsafe_placeholder' (today's existing category="alternative_requirement", concept_id=None conservative fallback) | 'baseline_unaffected' (NONE-structure text that must flow through the ordinary per-claim pipeline exactly as before M10D) | 'unsupported_mixed' (current JobRequirement/parser design CAN express this as independent_rows + one any_of_group together, but no M10D candidate below attempts the AND/OR boundary detection this requires -- see docs/evaluation/MILESTONE_10D_ALTERNATIVE_SEMANTICS.md Phase 6 Root Cause 6)
schema_notes.unsupported_by_current_model: true iff no annotated expected outcome is representable as a single logical JobRequirement shape at all (there is none in this corpus -- MIXED cases ARE representable as independent_rows + any_of_group together, just not by any candidate implemented here)
